fullPassage:
Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your listener?
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, __________.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ a better / can / anyone / listener / become ]
questions.wa: anyone can become a better listener
accept: anyone can become a better listener
Anyone can become a better listener
anyone can become a better listener.

det.korean: 누구든 더 나은 청자가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ anyone(주어) + can become(동사) + a better listener(보어).
det.tip: anyone = 누구든. become a better listener = 더 나은 청자가 되다. can = 할 수 있다.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by ①<u>creating</u> a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or ②<u>evaluate</u> others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will ③<u>appreciate</u> when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a ④<u>well</u> listener.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 누구든 더 나은(better) 청자가 될 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①creating: by + V-ing 정상. ✅ ②evaluate: discuss or evaluate(병렬) 정상. ✅ ③appreciate: will appreciate(미래형) 정상. ❌ ④well: a well listener(X). 관사+형용사+명사 구조에서 well은 부사. 원문은 a better listener. better(형용사)가 맞음.
det.tip: well(부사) vs better(형용사). a better listener = 더 나은 청자. 관사+형용사+명사.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are ①<u>laughing</u> over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be ②<u>working</u> on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a ③<u>supportive</u> look on his face; he is actually waiting for you ④<u>give</u> your presentation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 당신이 발표를 하기를 기다리고 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①laughing: are laughing(진행형) 정상. ✅ ②working: seems to be working(진행형) 정상. ✅ ③supportive: supportive look(형용사+명사) 정상. ❌ ④give: wait for + O + to V. waiting for you to give가 맞음. to 누락.
det.tip: wait for + 목적어 + to V. give(X) → to give(O). for you give는 불가.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech ①<u>that</u> interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some ②<u>techniques</u> that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be ③<u>constructive</u> and helpful. Listening well is ④<u>so</u> important as speaking well.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①that: 관계대명사 주격(something that interests you) 정상. ✅ ②techniques: 복수형 정상. ✅ ③constructive: be constructive(보어) 정상. ❌ ④so: 원문은 as important as(원급비교). so ~ as는 부정문에서만 사용 가능. 긍정문에서는 as ~ as가 맞음.
det.tip: as + 형용사 + as(원급비교, 긍정문). so ~ as는 부정문 한정. so important as(X) → as important as(O).

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some ①<u>techniques</u> that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an ②<u>attitude</u> you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as ③<u>important</u> as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a ④<u>worse</u> listener.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 누구든 더 나은(better) 청자가 될 수 있다. worse(더 나쁜)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①techniques: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②attitude: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③important: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④worse: 원문은 better. 'Fortunately'(다행히)라는 긍정 부사와 worse(더 나쁜)는 모순.
det.tip: better(더 나은) ↔ worse(더 나쁜). Fortunately = 다행히 → 긍정적 결과.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a ①<u>supportive</u> look on his face; he is actually ②<u>waiting</u> for you to give your presentation. Who would you like to have as your ③<u>listener</u>? Good listeners can help ④<u>opponents</u> by creating a positive communication climate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 좋은 청자는 화자(speakers)를 도울 수 있다. opponents(상대방)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①supportive: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②waiting: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③listener: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④opponents: 원문은 speakers. 청자가 도와야 할 대상은 화자.
det.tip: speakers(화자) ↔ opponents(상대방/적). 경청의 맥락에서 화자를 돕는 것이 적절.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen __________ and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 주의 깊게 듣고 흥미로운 것을 찾아야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②carefully: 원문 'listen carefully'. 주의 깊게. ❌ ①reluctantly(마지못해): 긍정적 맥락에 부적합. ❌ ③briefly(짧게): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ④randomly(무작위로): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: carefully = 주의 깊게, 신중히. 경청의 핵심 태도.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 학생은 숙제를 하고 있는 것 같다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③homework: 원문 'working on her homework'. ❌ ①presentation(발표): 화자가 하는 것. ❌ ②cellphone(휴대폰): 앞줄 학생이 쓰는 것. ❌ ④speech(연설): 맥락 불일치.
det.tip: work on homework = 숙제를 하다. 발표 중 딴짓하는 학생 중 하나.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. That is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to __________ you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 남들이 네 말을 들어주길 원하는 대로 들어라.
det.analysis: ✅ ④listen to: 원문 'as you would want them to listen to you'. 황금률의 핵심. ❌ ①criticize(비판하다): 맥락 반대. ❌ ②entertain(즐겁게 하다): 무관. ❌ ③evaluate(평가하다): 경청과 다름.
det.tip: Golden Rule: 네가 대접받고 싶은 대로 남을 대접하라. listen to = 귀 기울이다.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 구석의 두 학생은 숙제를 함께 하고 있다
한 학생이 지지하는 표정으로 발표를 기다리고 있다
앞줄 학생은 발표 내용을 메모하고 있다

det.korean: 지지하는 표정으로 발표를 기다리는 학생이 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting'. ❌ ①: 웃고 있음, 숙제 아님. ❌ ③: 문자 보내는 중, 메모 아님. ❌ ④: 대부분 딴짓.
det.tip: supportive look = 지지하는 표정. 유일하게 경청 준비된 학생.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 좋은 청자는 긍정적인 소통 분위기를 만들 수 있다
관심 없는 주제에서는 얻을 것이 없다
다른 사람의 발표를 평가할 때 건설적이어야 한다

det.korean: 관심 없어도 유용한 기법을 습득할 수 있다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③: 'Even if you are not excited... you may pick up some techniques' → 관심 없어도 얻을 것이 있다. ✅ ①②④: 원문 일치.
det.tip: Even if = ~하더라도. 양보의 접속사. 관심 없어도 기법을 배울 수 있다.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 좋은 청자가 되기 위한 태도와 경청의 황금률

det.korean: 좋은 청자가 되기 위한 태도와 경청의 황금률.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: good listeners + listen carefully + Golden Rule of Listening. ❌ ②: 발표 기법이 아닌 경청. ❌ ③: 말하기가 아닌 듣기 중심. ❌ ④: 수업 집중이 아닌 경청 일반.
det.tip: 글의 핵심 키워드: listeners, listen carefully, Golden Rule of Listening.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation. <u>Who would you like to have as your listener?</u>
questions.stem: 위 글에서 밑줄 친 문장이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 발표할 때 친구를 청중으로 초대해야 한다
경청하는 자세를 가진 학생이 이상적인 청자이다
발표자는 자신이 원하는 청중만 선택할 수 있다

det.korean: 경청하는 자세를 가진 학생이 이상적인 청자라는 의미.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: 딴짓하는 학생들 vs 지지하는 표정의 학생 대비. 마지막 학생이 이상적 청자. ❌ ①: 친구 초대가 아님. ❌ ②: 수가 아닌 자세가 핵심. ❌ ④: 선택이 아닌 이상적 태도 제시.
det.tip: 수사의문문: 대답을 구하는 것이 아니라 경청 태도의 중요성을 강조.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak. When you discuss or evaluate others' speeches, be constructive and helpful. <u>That</u> is an attitude you will appreciate when others comment on your speech.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'That'이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 건설적이고 도움이 되는 태도를 갖는 것

det.korean: That = 건설적이고 도움이 되는 태도.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'be constructive and helpful' → That. 바로 앞 문장의 내용을 가리킴. ❌ ①: 흥미는 earlier 맥락. ❌ ③: 기법 습득은 별개. ❌ ④: 비판은 constructive와 반대.
det.tip: That은 앞 문장 전체 내용을 지칭. be constructive and helpful = 건설적이고 도움이 되는.

questions.passage: Imagine you are giving a presentation in class. As you stand before the class, you see the following: A student in the front row is texting on his cell phone. Two students in the corner are laughing over something they are holding under their desks. Another student seems to be working on her homework. Finally, here is a student who seems ready to listen. <u>He</u> has a supportive look on his face; he is actually waiting for you to give your presentation.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'He'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: He = 들을 준비가 된 학생.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 'a student who seems ready to listen. He has a supportive look.' He = 경청 준비된 학생. ❌ ①②③: 각각 딴짓하는 학생들.
det.tip: He는 바로 앞 a student who seems ready to listen을 받는 대명사.

questions.passage: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate. As a listener, you should listen carefully and look for something in the speech that interests you. Even if you are not excited about the topic, you may pick up some techniques that will be useful when it is your time to speak.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"주제에 관심이 없더라도 나중에 유용할 __________을/를 습득할 수 있다."

det.korean: 유용할 기법(techniques)을 습득할 수 있다.
det.analysis: ✅ techniques: 'pick up some techniques that will be useful'에서 직접 찾기.
det.tip: techniques = 기법, 기술. pick up techniques = 기법을 습득하다.

questions.passage: Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

She is a very __________ (support) friend who always listens to me.

det.korean: 그녀는 매우 지지하는/격려하는 친구이다.
det.analysis: ✅ supportive: a very __________ friend → 형용사 필요. support(동사/명사) → supportive(형용사).
det.tip: support(동사/명사) → supportive(형용사: 지지하는, 격려하는).

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"남들이 네 말을 들어주길 원하는 대로 남의 말을 들어라."

조건: listen, others, want, them을 사용할 것
questions.wa: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you
accept: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you
Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
listen to others as you would want them to listen to you

det.korean: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
det.analysis: ✅ Listen to others(명령문) + as(접속사: ~처럼) + you would want(가정법 과거) + them to listen to you(5형식).
det.tip: as you would want: 네가 원하듯이. want + O + to V: ~가 ~하길 원하다.

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"좋은 청자는 긍정적인 소통 분위기를 만들어 화자를 도울 수 있다."

조건: listeners, help, creating, positive, communication을 사용할 것
questions.wa: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate
accept: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate
Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate.
good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate

det.korean: Good listeners can help speakers by creating a positive communication climate.
det.analysis: ✅ Good listeners(주어) + can help(동사) + speakers(목적어) + by creating(수단) + a positive communication climate(목적어).
det.tip: by + V-ing: ~함으로써. communication climate = 소통 분위기.

questions.passage: Listening well is as important as speaking well. Fortunately, anyone can become a better listener. Just remember the Golden Rule of Listening: Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 좋은 청자가 되는 것은 타고난 능력으로만 가능하다.
잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다.

det.korean: 잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다 (as important as speaking well)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 잘 듣는 것은 잘 말하는 것만큼 중요하다. — 원문: 'Listening well is as important as speaking well'
❌ ① 경청이 덜 중요하다 — 원문: as important as(동등)
❌ ② 타고난 능력 — 원문: 'anyone can become a better listener'
❌ ④ 비판적으로 듣기 — 원문: 'Listen to others as you would want them to listen to you'
det.tip: as important as = ~만큼 중요한. 원급 비교.
